title: Services & Errands
subtitle: Handle the post office, the hairdresser's and repairs in French

lessons.title: À la poste
lessons.description: Send parcels and letters, buy stamps, fill in forms and track a delivery at the French post office.

blocks.heading: At the counter
blocks.body: In a French post office you take a ticket, wait for your number, then go to the counter (le guichet). Start with a polite greeting and say what you need with « Je voudrais… ». The clerk will ask a few standard questions about weight, speed and insurance.

examples.french: Bonjour, je voudrais envoyer ce colis en Espagne.
examples.english: Hello, I'd like to send this parcel to Spain.

examples.french: C'est à quel guichet, s'il vous plaît ?
examples.english: Which counter is it at, please?

examples.french: Je voudrais un carnet de timbres.

examples.french: Vous voulez l'envoyer en recommandé ?

examples.french: Il y a beaucoup de monde, je fais la queue.
examples.english: There are a lot of people, I'm queuing.

blocks.tip: In France the post office is called La Poste, and its yellow logo is everywhere — even on small village shops that host a postal counter.

blocks.heading: Weight, price and speed
blocks.body: The clerk weighs your parcel (peser) and gives you a price based on the weight (le poids) and the delivery speed. You usually choose between a normal service and an express one. Numbers with grammes and kilos come up constantly.

examples.french: Je peux le peser, s'il vous plaît ?
examples.english: Can I weigh it, please?

examples.french: Le colis fait deux kilos trois cents.
examples.english: The parcel weighs two kilos three hundred.

examples.french: Le tarif normal, c'est huit euros quatre-vingts.

examples.english: By express, it arrives tomorrow before midday.

examples.french: C'est plus cher, mais c'est plus rapide.

blocks.tip: Prices are often given as « huit euros quatre-vingts » — the word centimes is usually left out.

blocks.heading: Forms and tracking
blocks.body: For a registered letter or a parcel going abroad you fill in a form (remplir un formulaire) with the sender and the recipient. Then you get a receipt with a tracking number so you can follow the parcel online.

examples.english: Fill in this form, please.

examples.french: Écrivez l'adresse du destinataire ici.

examples.french: J'ai suivi mon colis sur Internet.

blocks.tip: Bring a pièce d'identité: for a recommandé or to collect a parcel, the clerk will always ask for ID.

blocks.heading: Polite requests: je voudrais, pourriez-vous
blocks.body: At a counter, French speakers avoid the blunt « je veux » (I want). Use « je voudrais » (I would like) + a noun or an infinitive. For asking someone to do something, « pourriez-vous » or « est-ce que je peux… ? » sound friendly and correct. These are conditional forms — at A2 you can simply learn them as fixed polite formulas.

examples.french: Je voudrais envoyer ce colis, s'il vous plaît.
examples.english: I'd like to send this parcel, please.

examples.french: Je voudrais deux timbres pour l'Allemagne.
examples.english: I'd like two stamps for Germany.

examples.english: Could you weigh my packet?

examples.french: Je voudrais savoir où est mon colis.
examples.english: I'd like to know where my parcel is.

blocks.tip: « Je veux » is not rude between friends, but at a counter it sounds abrupt. Je voudrais is always safe.

blocks.heading: Pronouns: le / la / les and lui / leur
blocks.body: To avoid repeating the parcel or the person, use a pronoun before the verb. Direct objects (things) become le, la, l', les. Indirect objects (to a person) become lui (to him/her) and leur (to them). In the passé composé the pronoun goes before the auxiliary: je l'ai envoyé.

examples.french: Ce colis ? Je l'envoie demain.
examples.english: This parcel? I'm sending it tomorrow.

examples.french: Les cartes postales, je les ai postées ce matin.
examples.english: The postcards, I posted them this morning.

examples.french: J'écris à ma sœur : je lui envoie une lettre.

examples.french: Mes parents adorent les photos, je leur envoie un album.
examples.english: My parents love photos, I'm sending them an album.

examples.french: Le formulaire ? La postière me l'a donné.
examples.english: The form? The postwoman gave it to me.

blocks.tip: Ask yourself: à + person? Then it's lui or leur. No à? Then it's le, la or les.

passages.title: Un colis pour Marseille
passages.french:
Samedi matin, Camille est allée à la poste avec un gros paquet pour sa cousine.
Il y avait beaucoup de monde et elle a fait la queue pendant vingt minutes.
Au guichet, l'employé a pesé le colis : trois kilos deux cents.
« En tarif normal, il arrive jeudi ; en express, mardi », a-t-il expliqué.
Camille a choisi le tarif normal parce que l'express coûtait douze euros de plus.
Elle a rempli un formulaire avec l'adresse et le code postal de sa cousine.
Elle a aussi acheté un carnet de timbres pour ses cartes postales.
L'employé lui a donné un reçu avec un numéro de suivi.
Le soir, Camille a suivi son colis sur Internet : il était déjà à Lyon.
Sa cousine l'a reçu jeudi matin, exactement comme prévu.
passages.english:
On Saturday morning, Camille went to the post office with a big package for her cousin.
There were a lot of people and she queued for twenty minutes.
At the counter, the clerk weighed the parcel: three kilos two hundred.
"At the normal rate, it arrives Thursday; by express, Tuesday," he explained.
Camille chose the normal rate because express cost twelve euros more.
She filled in a form with her cousin's address and postcode.
She also bought a book of stamps for her postcards.
The clerk gave her a receipt with a tracking number.
In the evening, Camille tracked her parcel online: it was already in Lyon.
Her cousin received it on Thursday morning, exactly as planned.

questions.prompt: Why did Camille choose the normal rate?
options: Because express was twelve euros more expensive
Because express was not available on Saturday
Because the parcel was too heavy for express
Because her cousin asked for the normal rate
questions.answer: Because express was twelve euros more expensive

questions.prompt: Camille a attendu vingt minutes avant d'arriver au guichet.
Où était le colis le samedi soir ?
options: Encore à la poste de Camille

lessons.title: Chez le coiffeur
lessons.description: Book an appointment at the hairdresser's and describe exactly what you want done.

blocks.heading: Booking the appointment
blocks.body: Most French salons work on appointment (sur rendez-vous), though some take walk-ins. On the phone you say who you are, what you want, and when you are free. The receptionist offers a slot and you confirm or ask for another one.

examples.french: Bonjour, je voudrais prendre rendez-vous pour une coupe.
examples.english: Hello, I'd like to make an appointment for a haircut.

examples.french: Vous avez quelque chose jeudi après-midi ?
examples.english: Do you have anything Thursday afternoon?

examples.french: Je suis disponible après dix-sept heures.
examples.english: I'm available after five p.m.

examples.french: C'est à quel nom ?
examples.english: What name is it under?

examples.french: Je dois annuler mon rendez-vous de samedi.
examples.english: I have to cancel my Saturday appointment.

blocks.tip: Salons often ask « C'est pour une coupe ou une couleur ? » — the price and the length of the slot depend on it.

blocks.heading: Saying what you want
blocks.body: Once you sit down, describe the result you want. Use « je voudrais » plus a noun, or « juste » (just) to keep things small. Quantities help a lot: un peu, deux centimètres, pas trop court.

examples.french: Je voudrais juste rafraîchir les pointes.
examples.english: I'd just like to freshen up the ends.

examples.french: Coupez deux centimètres, s'il vous plaît.
examples.english: Cut off two centimetres, please.

examples.french: Pas trop court sur les côtés.
examples.english: Not too short on the sides.

examples.french: Je préfère garder la frange longue.
examples.english: I'd rather keep the fringe long.

examples.french: Est-ce que vous pouvez faire un brushing après ?
examples.english: Can you do a blow-dry afterwards?

examples.french: La dernière fois, c'était un peu trop court.
examples.english: Last time it was a little too short.

blocks.tip: « Un peu » is your safety word: « juste un peu, s'il vous plaît » prevents most haircut disasters.

blocks.heading: Colour, beard and paying
blocks.body: Colouring (la coloration) is booked separately and takes longer. Men's salons also offer beard trimming. At the end you pay at the desk; a small tip is welcome but never obligatory in France.

blocks.tip: Tipping is optional: leaving two or three euros for a good cut is generous, not expected.

blocks.heading: se faire couper les cheveux
blocks.body: In French you do not say « je coupe mes cheveux » unless you really cut them yourself. When someone else does it for you, use se faire + infinitive: je me fais couper les cheveux. Note that the body part takes le / la / les, not a possessive. In the passé composé, the past participle fait never agrees: elle s'est fait couper les cheveux.

blocks.tip: Same structure for other services: se faire faire les ongles, se faire livrer un colis.

blocks.heading: trop, assez, un peu and comparisons
blocks.body: To describe how short or how long you want something, put a small word in front of the adjective: trop (too), assez (fairly), un peu (a bit), pas trop (not too). To compare with last time, use plus… que (more… than) and moins… que (less… than).

examples.english: Today it's less short than last time.

blocks.tip: « Un peu plus court » (a little shorter) is the single most useful phrase in a salon.

passages.title: Un rendez-vous chez le coiffeur
passages.french:
Lundi, Julien a téléphoné au salon de coiffure de son quartier.
Il voulait un rendez-vous le mercredi soir, mais tout était complet.
La coiffeuse lui a proposé jeudi à dix-huit heures et il a accepté.
Jeudi, il est arrivé cinq minutes en avance et il a attendu dans un fauteuil.
Après le shampoing, la coiffeuse a demandé : « Comment je vous coupe les cheveux ? »
Julien a répondu qu'il voulait garder les cheveux longs devant.
« Juste deux centimètres, et pas trop court sur les côtés », a-t-il précisé.
À la fin, elle a fait un brushing rapide et lui a montré la nuque dans le miroir.
Julien était content : c'était moins court que la dernière fois.
Il a payé vingt-huit euros et il a laissé deux euros de pourboire.
passages.english:
On Monday, Julien phoned the hair salon in his neighbourhood.
He wanted an appointment on Wednesday evening, but everything was full.
The hairdresser offered him Thursday at six p.m. and he accepted.
On Thursday he arrived five minutes early and waited in an armchair.
After the shampoo, the hairdresser asked: "How shall I cut your hair?"
Julien answered that he wanted to keep his hair long at the front.
"Just two centimetres, and not too short on the sides," he specified.
At the end, she did a quick blow-dry and showed him the nape in the mirror.
Julien was happy: it was less short than last time.
He paid twenty-eight euros and left a two-euro tip.

lessons.title: Réparations
lessons.description: Get things repaired, cleaned and altered, using faire + infinitive to say you have it done.

blocks.heading: Explaining the problem
blocks.body: Start by saying what is wrong. Very common phrases: ça ne marche plus (it doesn't work any more), c'est cassé (it's broken), il y a une tache (there's a stain). Say when the problem started if you can — the repairer will ask.

examples.french: Bonjour, mon téléphone ne marche plus.
examples.english: Hello, my phone doesn't work any more.

examples.french: L'écran est cassé depuis hier.
examples.english: The screen has been broken since yesterday.

examples.french: Ma machine à laver est en panne.
examples.english: My washing machine is out of order.

examples.french: Il y a une tache de café sur la veste.
examples.english: There's a coffee stain on the jacket.

examples.french: La fermeture éclair est bloquée.
examples.english: The zip is stuck.

blocks.tip: « Ça ne marche plus » is the everyday way to say something has stopped working — it covers phones, cars and coffee machines.

blocks.heading: At the dry cleaner's
blocks.body: Le pressing takes clothes for dry cleaning (le nettoyage à sec) and often does small alterations too. You leave the item, get a ticket, and come back on the date written on it.

examples.french: Je voudrais faire nettoyer ce manteau.
examples.english: I'd like to have this coat cleaned.

examples.french: C'est prêt pour vendredi ?
examples.english: Will it be ready by Friday?

examples.french: Gardez bien le ticket, s'il vous plaît.
examples.english: Please keep the ticket.

examples.french: Vous faites aussi les retouches ?
examples.english: Do you do alterations as well?

examples.french: Le pantalon est trop long, il faut faire un ourlet.
examples.english: The trousers are too long, they need a hem.

blocks.tip: Ask « Vous pensez que la tache va partir ? » — literally "do you think the stain will go away?"

blocks.heading: Price, delay and guarantee
blocks.body: For anything expensive, ask for an estimate (un devis) before the work starts. Check the delay (le délai) and whether the item is still under warranty (sous garantie), because that can make the repair free.

examples.french: Vous pouvez me faire un devis ?
examples.english: Can you give me an estimate?

examples.french: Ça coûte combien, la réparation ?
examples.english: How much does the repair cost?

examples.french: Le délai est de cinq jours ouvrables.
examples.english: The turnaround time is five working days.

examples.french: L'appareil est encore sous garantie.
examples.english: The device is still under warranty.

examples.french: Je passe le récupérer mardi, alors.
examples.english: I'll come and pick it up on Tuesday, then.

blocks.tip: « Jours ouvrables » means working days — weekends and holidays don't count.

blocks.heading: faire + infinitive: having something done
blocks.body: English says "I'm having my bike repaired". French says faire + infinitive: je fais réparer mon vélo. The verb faire is conjugated normally and the second verb stays in the infinitive. The object comes after the infinitive: faire réparer le vélo, faire nettoyer la veste. In the passé composé, the participle fait never agrees: j'ai fait réparer mes chaussures.

examples.french: Je fais réparer mon téléphone demain.
examples.english: I'm having my phone repaired tomorrow.

examples.french: Nous faisons nettoyer les rideaux au pressing.
examples.english: We're having the curtains cleaned at the dry cleaner's.

examples.french: Il a fait changer la batterie de sa voiture.
examples.english: He had the battery of his car changed.

examples.french: Tu devrais faire recoudre ce bouton.
examples.english: You should have this button sewn back on.

examples.french: Elle va faire raccourcir sa robe.
examples.english: She's going to have her dress shortened.

blocks.tip: Compare: « je répare mon vélo » = I fix it myself; « je fais réparer mon vélo » = someone else fixes it for me.

blocks.heading: Saying it stopped working: ne… plus and depuis
blocks.body: To say something no longer works, put ne… plus around the verb: ça ne marche plus. To say how long the problem has lasted, use depuis + a moment (depuis lundi) or depuis + a length of time (depuis trois jours) with the present tense.

examples.french: Le lave-vaisselle ne marche plus.
examples.english: The dishwasher doesn't work any more.

examples.french: Ma montre ne fonctionne plus depuis samedi.
examples.english: My watch hasn't worked since Saturday.

examples.french: L'écran est cassé depuis deux semaines.
examples.english: The screen has been broken for two weeks.

examples.french: Je n'ai plus de garantie sur cet appareil.
examples.english: I no longer have a warranty on this device.

examples.french: Il n'y a plus de pièces de rechange pour ce modèle.
examples.english: There are no more spare parts for this model.

blocks.tip: French keeps the present tense with depuis where English uses "has been": j'attends depuis dix minutes = I've been waiting for ten minutes.

passages.title: Une journée de courses
passages.french:
Samedi, Nadia avait trois choses à faire dans son quartier.
D'abord, elle est allée au pressing avec la veste de son mari.
Il y avait une tache de café sur la manche depuis le mariage de son frère.
« Je pense que ça va partir », a dit l'employée en lui donnant un ticket.
Ensuite, Nadia est passée chez le cordonnier pour faire changer un talon.
Le cordonnier a regardé la chaussure et a proposé aussi de recoller la semelle.
Enfin, elle a apporté son téléphone à l'atelier de réparation, près du marché.
L'écran était cassé depuis une semaine et l'appareil n'était plus sous garantie.
Le technicien a fait un devis gratuit : quatre-vingts euros, prêt mercredi.
Nadia a accepté, parce qu'un téléphone neuf coûtait beaucoup plus cher.
passages.english:
On Saturday, Nadia had three things to do in her neighbourhood.
First, she went to the dry cleaner's with her husband's jacket.
There had been a coffee stain on the sleeve since her brother's wedding.
"I think it will come out," said the assistant, giving her a ticket.
Then Nadia stopped at the cobbler's to have a heel changed.
The cobbler looked at the shoe and also offered to glue the sole back on.
Finally, she took her phone to the repair workshop near the market.
The screen had been broken for a week and the device was no longer under warranty.
The technician gave a free estimate: eighty euros, ready on Wednesday.
Nadia accepted, because a new phone cost a lot more.

questions.answer: Because a new phone was much more expensive
